messages:
Priya: FYI customers flagged a weird spike in quota usage for routes after the TS SDK v2.1.0 rollout. Looks like attribution is split across two route keys.
Ben: Spike how big? whole tenant or specific route?
Priya: Specific route `alpha/inbox` on a test tenant. Quota graph shows parallel burns in `alpha/inbox` and `alpha/_fallback`.
Liam: Could be the new header rename we shipped in v2.1.0 (`X-Route-ID` -> `X-Route-Id`) causing the console normalizer to treat as different keys.
Priya: I compared the raw events: some requests have `X-Route-ID: alpha%2Finbox` and others `X-Route-Id: alpha/inbox` (URL-decoding mismatch).
Ben: Oof. So two problems: casing change and encoding variance.
Console-UX: We show route keys raw right now; no normalization. Might be worth normalizing both header name and decoding.
Priya: Repro: curl with encoded header vs plain:
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Route-ID: alpha%2Finbox" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
and
```
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-Route-Id: alpha/inbox" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}' \
  https://api.staging.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
Ben: Why did SDK change header casing? Was that intentional in the fetch shim?
Liam: It was an accidental normalization in the client adapter (ts-http): we lowercased headers and then camel-cased them when constructing; inconsistent behavior across node and browser.
Priya: Impact: hosted customers see split quotas, Dedicated ones might be fine because their proxies canonicalize. But still bad.
Ben: Quick mitigations?
Liam: Short-term: console layer can canonicalize route keys by lowercasing header names and URL-decoding values, and then merge buckets for a 24h window. Low-risk hotfix.
Console-UX: We can also add an alert banner when a merged key has >5% discrepancy so customers know we merged.
Priya: Medium-term: patch TS SDK to send a canonical header `X-Route-Canonical: tenant/alpha/inbox` always, and stop renaming existing header. This is a minor bump.
Ben: SDK patch timeline?
Liam: I can cut a v2.1.1 today with the fix, release tomorrow. Add unit tests for header canonicalization.
Priya: Telemetry-wise we should emit a stable field `route_canonical` in the event payload so console and billing can join on that instead of relying on header names.
Ben: Agree. Also add a small repro integration test that simulates both header forms to ensure console dedupe.
Liam: Ops note: for Dedicated customers we need to ensure proxies don't URL-encode route ids. I'll open OPS ticket.
Priya: Can ops also run a one-off job to reconcile historical double-counted tokens for the last 48h? Some customers reported cost variance.
Ben: Reconciliation needs product signoff but we can prepare a diff export.
Priya: I'll loop in Product. File references: console-hotfix PR #5008, sdk bugfix #2550, ops ticket OPS-802, telemetry event issue #618.
Console-UX: I'll ship the banner and merging logic behind `redwood.console.merge_route_aliases` feature flag and enable it for hosted staging canary.
ops-bot: deploybot: staging canary for console-route-merge started at 1719010300, smoke tests OK.
Liam: Adding unit tests and changelog entry. Also will include migration note in SDK release notes about header canonicalization.
Priya: Thanks all. Plan: console hotfix -> canary -> rollout, SDK v2.1.1 release, ops proxy changes, telemetry event follow-up. Revisit in ~1h (1719010620) for metrics check.
Ben: Thanks. We'll monitor billing alerts and search for other header-name edgecases.
Priya: Filed items in links channel and pinged a couple customers privately.
Console-UX: thumbs up.
